verification_note: The six SRS files named in detail_files (plus this index) are the deliverable. The repository also contains _verification/validate.py, which is NOT an SRS document and is deliberately absent from detail_files: it is a reconciliation harness that re-derives every count in this index from the detail files, checks that every cited REQ / NFR / ANOM / MOD / entity / state identifier resolves, verifies state-machine reachability and exit conditions, asserts that no optional field carries a null literal, and asserts that the six intentional requirement-vs-anomaly action divergences match the declared set. It could not be executed in this dispatch because the sandbox withheld approval for running Python, so every count in this document set was instead reconciled by two independent full-read verification passes. Those passes found and corrected five arithmetic defects: summary.total_transitions (31 -> 29), anomaly by_type (data_integrity_risk 5 -> 6, duplicate_logic 3 -> 2), anomaly by_source (four of six buckets wrong), the data-model attribute provenance split (5/28 -> 10/23), and verification.source_coverage.implicit_logic_flagged_requires_sme_review (11 -> 14, since confirmed as 14 directly against implicit-logic.json). A reviewer with permission to run Python should execute the harness to confirm; it is the cheapest available check on this document set's internal consistency.

Where no identifier exists upstream, the citation is a JSON path into the source artifact (e.g. 'structural-analysis.json:coupling_indicators.magic_string_dispatch').

modules.name: Inventory Revaluation Rules Engine
modules.description: The per-item-category rules that adjust quality and sell_in once per revaluation cycle, and the bounds that constrain them. This is the whole of the legacy application's business logic: 75 lines in one method, src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:37-111. In the prescribed design it becomes an independently invocable module (REQ-028) whose rules are data on a category definition rather than nested name comparisons.
modules.requirement_ids_selector: srs-requirements-functional.json: requirements[?module_hint=='MOD-001'] -> REQ-001..REQ-016, REQ-018, REQ-028 (18). srs-requirements-nonfunctional.json: requirements[?module_hint=='MOD-001'] -> NFR-006, NFR-007, NFR-009, NFR-010 (4).
notable_findings: BR-016 / IL-009 — sell_in means two different things within one iteration; the only high-complexity rule in the catalogue, severity critical, and the change most likely to be silently broken by a refactor. Resolved as ANOM-001.
BR-017 / IL-007 / QR-005 — the entire business taxonomy is eight case-sensitive comparisons against customer-facing display names. Resolved as ANOM-002.
BR-MISSING-001 / IL-024 — the documented Conjured rule is absent from the code while a Conjured item sits in live inventory; mispriced on every run. Resolved as ANOM-018.

BR-003 / IL-002 — the quality floor is a guard rather than a clamp and holds only because every legacy decrement is exactly 1; REQ-018 introduces the first multi-step degradation, which would break it. Resolved as ANOM-003.

IL-012 — the concert-day bonus is computed and discarded, and the churn repeats forever on an expired pass; harmless in the legacy system, a correctness defect once REQ-025/REQ-027 make intermediates observable. Resolved as ANOM-007.

modules.name: Item Catalog and Domain Model
modules.description: The inventory item, its explicit category, and the validation that admits it. The legacy counterpart is a three-property POCO with public setters and no invariants (Program.cs:115-122) plus a latent, code-less category taxonomy that data-domains.json records as domain DD-GRK-002 with physical_footprint 'NONE, and not even a data structure'. This module is where boundary validation lives, so inner layers can trust their input.
modules.requirement_ids_selector: srs-requirements-functional.json: requirements[?module_hint=='MOD-002'] -> REQ-017, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-021.
notable_findings: BR-018 / IL-019 / QR-008 — the model enforces no invariants; quality -100 or 9999 constructs cleanly and is never normalized. Resolved as ANOM-011.

BR-023 / IL-021 — a null, empty or unrecognised name raises no exception and silently depreciates as standard goods, with no log entry anywhere to leave a trace. Resolved as ANOM-010 (a deliberate behaviour change requiring SME sign-off).
BR-022 / IL-020 — sell_in has no floor and no archival path; only its sign is ever tested. Resolved as ANOM-012.
IL-023 — the model has no quantity or stock-count field. DEFERRED as ANOM-025: prescribing one would be an invented feature with no discovery evidence.

modules.name: Revaluation Run Orchestration and Host
modules.description: What invokes a revaluation cycle, where the inventory comes from, which business date the cycle represents, and what happens to the result. The legacy counterpart is Program.Main (Program.cs:8-35): it seeds six compiled-in items, calls the rules once, prints nothing of the result, blocks on a keypress and exits. structural-analysis.json names this the 'inventory-run-host' decomposition boundary and identifies the two structural facts that must change — the blocking keypress and the non-parameterisable seed list.
modules.requirement_ids_selector: srs-requirements-functional.json: requirements[?module_hint=='MOD-003'] -> REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-024, REQ-025.
notable_findings: BR-020 / IL-016 / IL-017 — the business calendar IS the process lifecycle: no clock, no run-date record, no already-processed check, no lock. A retry after a partial failure would double-apply a day's depreciation in any variant that persisted its results — and REQ-025 makes this that variant. Resolved as ANOM-013.

IL-018 — the only output is a banner printed BEFORE the calculation; the revaluation's result is unobservable and dies with the process. data-domains.json records the same as BV-GRK-003 at severity high. Resolved as ANOM-015.
BR-021 — a blocking Console.ReadKey() means a nightly process cannot complete unattended; it hangs under an orchestrator. Resolved as ANOM-014.

BR-019 — the inventory is six items constructed inline in Main, and Main's args parameter is declared and never read (the application's only dead code, QR-007). Resolved as ANOM-019 (OMIT the vestigial parameter, prescribe a designed invocation contract).

modules.name: Access Control, Audit and Observability
modules.description: Who may run a revaluation, and what record survives of what it did. This module has NO legacy counterpart of any kind: identity-landscape.json confirms by negative grep over all 22 tracked files that there is no authentication code, no authorization check, no session, no user record and no credential store, and IL-025 records no before/after capture, no logging framework, no event and no versioning. Every requirement here adds a capability that does not exist today rather than modifying one.
modules.requirement_ids_selector: srs-requirements-functional.json: requirements[?module_hint=='MOD-004'] -> REQ-026, REQ-027. srs-requirements-nonfunctional.json: requirements[?module_hint=='MOD-004'] -> NFR-008.
notable_findings: BR-024 — the catalogue's single authorization rule, and it records the ABSENCE of any: no user, role, permission check or approval step governs revaluation of the entire inventory. Its regulatory note flags missing NIST 800-53 AC-3 access enforcement. Resolved as ANOM-016.

IL-025 — no audit trail: quality is mutated at 13 sites and sell_in at 1 with no before/after capture, so 'there is no way to answer why an item is worth what it is worth'. NIST 800-53 AU-2/AU-12 gap. Resolved as ANOM-017.

IL-022 / BR-024.test_hints — the rules engine's only access control today is accidental (public method on an internal class reading a private field). REQ-028 deliberately widens that seam to make the rules testable, which is precisely why REQ-026 must land in the same release: 'making the class or field more accessible during modernization would widen an unguarded mutation surface'.

modules.name: Platform, Build and Verification Quality
modules.description: The cross-cutting properties the modernized system must hold: a behavioural test baseline, a supported runtime, a hermetic build, dependency vulnerability scanning, and accessibility conformance. Grouped as a module because each is a system-wide obligation rather than a behaviour of any single functional area, and because quality-risk.json concentrates all 18 of its weighted smell occurrences and its entire 76/100 debt score in this application's single production module.

notable_findings: quality-risk.json test_coverage / IL-026 — 0% line and branch coverage of the rules engine, PROVEN structurally (no ProjectReference from the test project) rather than merely unmeasured. quality-risk.json's first top risk driver; IL-026 states this is 'what makes every implicit behaviour dangerous rather than merely untidy: nothing would fail if a re-implementation changed any of them'. actors.name: Inventory Operator
actors.authentication: PRESCRIBED: authenticated identity with the inventory:revalue permission, and a separate inventory:revalue:override permission for re-running a completed business date (REQ-026). LEGACY: none whatsoever — identity-landscape.json records model_name 'None — unauthenticated local console execution', provider 'none', and the sole access control as the operating system's own session, 'which this application never reads'.
actors.target_assurance: PRESCRIBED: phishing-resistant AAL2 or above (PIV or FIDO2). LEGACY MEASURED: nist_ial 'unknown', nist_aal 'below-AAL1', nist_fal 'not-applicable', mfa_type 'none', phishing_resistant false. The target is taken from identity-landscape.json's own remediation guidance for the modernized surface — 'require phishing-resistant AAL2+ (PIV or FIDO2) on the new surface and do not carry forward any email- or SMS-code pattern' — and NOT from the client profile, which was unreadable in this dispatch (see open_questions[2]).
endpoints_accessed: The revaluation invocation contract (REQ-022, REQ-023) — successor to the single legacy interface, 'GildedRose.Console.exe command-line invocation'

evidence.derivation: EVIDENCED AS EXISTING. identity-landscape.json user_classes names exactly one actor: 'local-interactive-operator (whoever holds an interactive Windows session on the host; identified and authorised solely by the OS login, which this application never reads)'. ux-accessibility.json independently derives the same single persona, 'local-console-operator (kata participant / build verifier)'. structural-analysis.json interface-inventory records the one interface as human_facing true, audience internal, authentication 'none'.
secondary_sources: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:33 (the blocking keypress — identity-landscape.json cites this as confirming 'an interactive local operator is the only actor')
src/GildedRose.Console/app.config:1-6 (no authentication, membership, roleManager, identity or authorization element exists)
evidence.authorization_check: NONE EXISTS. identity-landscape.json records that greps across all 22 tracked files for identity|principal|authenticat|authoriz|oauth|saml|ldap|login.gov|piv|password|credential|token returned only three false positives — the PublicKeyToken attributes on xUnit assembly references at GildedRose.Tests.csproj:46, :50 and :54. BR-024 records the same absence as its single authorization-category rule. This actor is therefore derived from the interface it uses and from the OS session that gates it, NOT from an authorization check, because no authorization check exists anywhere in the application to derive one from.
evidence.confidence: medium — the actor's EXISTENCE is well evidenced by three independent Discovery artifacts, but its permissions and assurance level are prescribed rather than observed, because the legacy system models neither. ux-accessibility.json separately rates its own persona inference confidence at 0.3 and raises the open review ask 'personas-confirmed', warning that if this application has real operational users beyond a kata participant, every persona-dependent downstream artifact rests on a fictional user base.

actors.name: Scheduled Revaluation Process
actors.authentication: PRESCRIBED: a non-interactive service identity (workload credential), authenticated and authorized against the inventory:revalue permission exactly as a human operator is (REQ-026), but through a distinct credential path with no interactive login. It MUST NOT hold the inventory:revalue:override permission — an override of a completed business date requires a named human decision per REQ-023.
actors.target_assurance: PRESCRIBED: workload identity with short-lived, automatically rotated credentials. Not applicable to the NIST AAL scale, which governs human authenticator assurance; recorded as such rather than given a borrowed AAL value.
endpoints_accessed: The revaluation invocation contract (REQ-022, REQ-023), invoked unattended per REQ-024

evidence.derivation: PRESCRIBED, NOT OBSERVED — AND DELIBERATELY KEPT SEPARATE FROM THE HUMAN ACTOR. No scheduler, timer, cron entry or service account exists anywhere in the legacy application: structural-analysis.json records scheduled_jobs 0, and IL-016 confirms 'no DateTime, timer, scheduler or date parameter exists anywhere'. This actor is nevertheless evidence-based rather than invented: BR-021 identifies the legacy system's central operational defect as the fact that 'a nightly inventory process therefore cannot complete unattended: in a scheduler or container it blocks indefinitely on a console that will never receive input', which names unattended scheduled execution as the intended mode of operation that the code prevents. structural-analysis.json's inventory-run-host decomposition boundary makes the same point structurally. REQ-024 prescribes that unattended completion, so the SRS must name the actor that performs it — otherwise REQ-024 has no subject and REQ-026 cannot state whose identity is authenticated. It is modelled as a SEPARATE actor rather than merged with Inventory Operator because its authentication path differs fundamentally (workload credential versus interactive human login) even though its revaluation permission overlaps.
secondary_sources: business-logic.json:BR-021 (interactive_keypress_blocks_unattended_execution, including its error_paths for scheduler and container hosts)
evidence.authorization_check: NONE EXISTS, and no scheduler exists either. Both the actor and its authorization are prescribed. Flagged for SME confirmation.
evidence.confidence: low — the NEED for unattended execution is well evidenced (BR-021 is explicit that the legacy design defeats it), but whether a scheduled process is the intended invoker, and on what cadence, is not established by any artifact. Depends on the ANOM-013 SME question: does a real inventory store exist outside this repository, and is one cycle per calendar day correct?

state_machines.name: ItemSellByLifecycle
state_machines.description: The master machine every non-LEGENDARY item traverses, driven solely by the sign of sell_in. PROVENANCE: reconstructed by Discovery, not declared in code — state-machines.json records that 'the application has no status field, no enum, no state column and no transition table', and that every machine was recovered from the thresholds the nested conditionals test. In this SRS these machines are PRESCRIPTIVE: they define the only valid transitions the modernized system may allow.

states.name: WithinSellByWindow
states.description: Pre-sell-by rules only.

states.name: FinalSellDay
states.description: The last cycle of single-rate treatment. state-machines.json calls this 'the most commonly mis-implemented boundary in the whole algorithm': the expiry test is FALSE here because sell_in after decrement is 0, not below 0.

states.name: PastSellBy
states.description: The past-sell-by rule set applies in addition to the pre-sell-by rules. Absorbing with respect to the sell-by dimension: no rule returns an item to an earlier state.

states.name: PastSellByArchivalEligible
states.definition: sell_in_after_decrement < 0 AND quality == 0 for the configured number of consecutive cycles
states.description: PRESCRIBED ADDITION (REQ-021). The legacy machine had no exit and no archival concept at all; this state makes a long-dead item visible to a business decision instead of decrementing forever.

transitions.action: decrement sell_in by 1; apply pre-sell-by quality rules
sell_in becomes 0; single-rate treatment still applies
sell_in becomes -1; the past-sell-by adjustment is applied in the same cycle

transitions.trigger: revaluation cycle while sell_in_at_cycle_start <= -1 and the archival threshold is not yet met
transitions.guard: category != LEGENDARY AND sell_in > configured floor
transitions.action: decrement sell_in by 1 down to the configured floor; apply the past-sell-by rule set

transitions.trigger: the configured number of consecutive cycles at quality 0 past the sell-by date is reached
transitions.action: set archival_eligible true; include the item in the cycle's archival-candidate report

traces_to.note: PRESCRIBED TRANSITION — no legacy counterpart. BR-022 and IL-020 record that nothing removes, archives or flags a long-expired item.

prescribed_changes: The legacy PastSellBy self-loop decremented sell_in without limit toward int.MinValue with no archival path (BR-022, IL-020). It is bounded by the configured floor and gains an exit to PastSellByArchivalEligible (REQ-021, ANOM-012).

The state is no longer recomputed from a single mutable field mid-cycle. Both sell_in_at_cycle_start and sell_in_after_decrement are named, and each transition states which it tests (REQ-016, ANOM-001). state-machines.json notes the legacy state 'is not stored; it is recomputed from SellIn on every iteration' — which is exactly what made BR-016 invisible.
state_machines.completeness_check: Every state is reachable from WithinSellByWindow. Every state has at least one exit transition except PastSellByArchivalEligible, which is intentionally absorbing within this SRS's scope: REQ-021 prescribes the FLAG but deliberately not the archival ACTION, and ANOM-012 records that the write-off owner is an open SME question. This is a scope boundary that is stated, not an undocumented dead end.

state_machines.name: StandardGoodsValuationLifecycle
state_machines.description: The quality trajectory of a STANDARD-category item: two degradation rates and one absorbing floor. In the legacy system this applied to '+5 Dexterity Vest', 'Elixir of the Mongoose' and — incorrectly, per BR-MISSING-001 — 'Conjured Mana Cake'. In the prescribed system the Conjured item is no longer routed here (REQ-018).

states.name: DepreciatingSingleRate
states.description: -1 quality per cycle.

states.name: DepreciatingDoubleRate
states.description: -2 quality per cycle, clamped at the floor — so from quality 1 the net loss is 1, not 2.

states.name: Worthless
states.description: Absorbing: no rule ever raises a standard good's quality.

transitions.action: apply the doubled degradation rate

transitions.trigger: quality reaches 0 while still within the sell-by window
transitions.action: clamp quality to 0

transitions.trigger: quality reaches 0 past the sell-by date
transitions.action: clamp quality to 0 — from quality 1 the net loss for the cycle is 1, not 2
quality stays 0; sell_in continues to fall toward the configured floor and the item becomes archival-eligible per REQ-021

prescribed_changes: The floor becomes a clamp on the computed result rather than two pre-decrement guards (REQ-003, ANOM-003). The quality-1 asymmetry is preserved deliberately and pinned by REQ-013's third acceptance criterion.
Conjured items no longer enter this machine; they have their own (REQ-018, ANOM-018).
state_machines.completeness_check: All three states reachable from DepreciatingSingleRate. Worthless is intentionally terminal in the quality dimension — state-machines.json confirms 'no rule ever raises a standard good's quality' — while the item remains subject to the sell-by machine, which is what carries it to archival eligibility.

state_machines.name: AppreciatingGoodsValuationLifecycle
state_machines.description: The quality trajectory of an APPRECIATING-category item (legacy exemplar 'Aged Brie'): the mirror image of the standard machine, with two appreciation rates and an absorbing ceiling.

states.name: AppreciatingSingleRate
states.description: +1 quality per cycle.

states.name: AppreciatingDoubleRate
states.description: +2 quality per cycle, clamped at the ceiling — so from quality 49 the net gain is 1, not 2. PRESCRIBED AS AN EXPLICIT RULE: state-machines.json records that in the legacy system 'the acceleration after the sell-by date is emergent — the business documentation states only that Brie improves with age, never that it improves faster once expired'.

states.name: Saturated
states.description: Absorbing under all code paths: nothing ever reduces an appreciating item's quality.

transitions.action: apply the doubled appreciation rate

transitions.trigger: quality reaches 50 while still within the sell-by window
transitions.action: clamp quality to 50

transitions.trigger: quality reaches 50 past the sell-by date
transitions.action: clamp quality to 50 — from quality 49 the net gain for the cycle is 1, not 2
quality stays 50; sell_in continues to fall toward the configured floor

prescribed_changes: The AppreciatingDoubleRate rate becomes an explicit expired_rate_per_cycle of 2 on the category definition rather than an emergent consequence of two increments firing in the same cycle (REQ-014, ANOM-009). SME confirmation required: no documentation asserts it.
The ceiling becomes one named constant and one clamp rather than the same literal at four sites (REQ-007, ANOM-004).
state_machines.completeness_check: All three states reachable from AppreciatingSingleRate. Saturated is intentionally terminal in the quality dimension. Note an asymmetry carried forward deliberately: a quality above 50 is unreachable by any rule but was constructible in the legacy model (IL-019); REQ-019 closes that at the boundary, so Saturated is genuinely the maximum in the prescribed system.

state_machines.name: BackstagePassValuationLifecycle
state_machines.description: The richest machine in the application: three demand tiers selected by sell-in proximity, an absorbing ceiling, and a cliff to zero when the event passes. state-machines.json records that every tier boundary is evaluated against the PRE-decrement sell_in, 'which is the only reason the literals 11 and 6 express 10 days or less and 5 days or less' — in this SRS those become inclusive comparisons against the named sell_in_at_cycle_start (REQ-016).

states.name: BaseDemand
states.description: +1 quality per cycle.

states.name: TenDayWindow
states.description: +2 quality per cycle (base plus the 10-day bonus).

states.name: FiveDayWindow
states.description: +3 quality per cycle (base plus both bonuses, each independently clamped).

states.name: Saturated
states.description: Reachable from any appreciating tier; exited only by the cliff to Worthless. state-machines.json notes that a pass worth the maximum 50 dropping to 0 in one cycle is 'the largest single-day value change the application can produce'.

states.name: Worthless
states.description: Quality 0. Absorbing.

transitions.action: apply base +1 plus the 10-day bonus +1
apply base +1 plus both bonuses, total +3
assign quality 0 directly. NO proximity bonus is computed for this cycle — the legacy compute-then-discard is removed (ANOM-007).
clamp quality to exactly 50; a pass eligible for +3 lands on 50 and never overshoots
clamp quality to exactly 50
assign quality 0 directly — the largest single-cycle value change the system can produce, from 50 to 0
NO adjustment is computed and quality remains 0. The legacy implicit-churn self-loop is removed (ANOM-007).

dead_states_removed.reason: COLLAPSED INTO A TRANSITION, NOT DELETED. state-machines.json models ConcertDay (sell_in == 0 at start of day) as a distinct state whose semantic is '+3 computed, then discarded — net Quality 0'. It exists as a state ONLY to describe the legacy compute-then-discard behaviour. Because REQ-015 prescribes that no bonus be computed for a pass whose sell-by date has passed (ANOM-007), there is no longer an intermediate condition to occupy a state: the concert day becomes the trigger of the FiveDayWindow-to-Worthless and Saturated-to-Worthless transitions. No behaviour is lost — the net observable outcome (quality 0) is identical.
dead_states_removed.evidence: state-machines.json:state_machines[BackstagePassValuationLifecycle].states[ConcertDay]; IL-012 ('concert_day_bonus_computed_then_discarded', Program.cs:53-73 then :99); BR-015 boundary condition 'SellIn 0 → -1: +3 applied then discarded, ending at 0'

dead_states_removed.state: Worthless implicit-churn self-loop (behaviour, not a state)
dead_states_removed.reason: REMOVED. state-machines.json documents the legacy Worthless-to-Worthless transition as 'IMPLICIT CHURN: the pass is still matched by the appreciation branch at line 41, so Quality rises 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 across lines 55, 63 and 71 (both thresholds are satisfied by a negative SellIn), and line 99 then zeroes it again.' It warns that 'a mid-iteration observer, a logger, or any re-implementation that splits these phases across transactions would see the non-zero intermediate'. Since REQ-025, REQ-027 and NFR-008 introduce exactly such a logger, audit and persistence boundary, the churn is removed rather than reproduced. The self-loop remains in the prescribed machine but performs no computation.

prescribed_changes: Tier thresholds are inclusive comparisons against the named sell_in_at_cycle_start (10 or fewer, 5 or fewer) rather than the bare literals 11 and 6 whose correctness depended on statement position (REQ-016, ANOM-001). IL-003 named the literal 11 'the single most likely mis-transcription in any re-implementation'.
The zeroing is a direct assignment of 0, not `Quality = Quality - Quality` (REQ-015, ANOM-008).
state_machines.completeness_check: All five states reachable from BaseDemand. Worthless is intentionally terminal. One reachability note recorded honestly: the direct BaseDemand-to-Saturated transition is unreachable in practice, because a pass at quality 49 or below gaining only +1 per cycle in BaseDemand must pass through TenDayWindow before it can reach 50 unless it is admitted at quality 50 already — in which case it is admitted directly into Saturated. It is therefore omitted rather than listed as a transition that cannot fire.

state_machines.name: ConjuredGoodsValuationLifecycle
state_machines.description: PRESCRIBED MACHINE WITH NO LEGACY IMPLEMENTATION. The quality trajectory of a CONJURED-category item: the standard-goods shape at double the rate. The legacy system has no such machine — state-machines.json recovered five machines and this is not among them, because the string 'Conjured' appears nowhere in UpdateQuality. A Conjured item exists in live inventory (Program.cs:26) and is currently routed through StandardGoodsValuationLifecycle, which is the mispricing BR-MISSING-001 records.

states.description: -2 quality per cycle, clamped at the floor.

states.name: DepreciatingQuadrupleRate
states.description: -4 quality per cycle, clamped at the floor.

states.name: Worthless
states.description: Absorbing.

transitions.action: clamp quality to 0 — from quality 1 a required -2 must land on 0, not -1

transitions.trigger: computed quality falls to 0 or below past the sell-by date

state_machines.name: LegendaryItemStasis
state_machines.description: DEGENERATE BY DESIGN, AND RECORDED BECAUSE ITS EMPTINESS IS THE FINDING. A LEGENDARY item has exactly one state and no transitions: its quality is exempt from every adjustment and its sell_in is never decremented, so it cannot leave the state it was admitted in.

states.name: PermanentStasis
states.description: sell_in and quality both frozen at their admitted values. In the prescribed system quality is additionally validated to equal the legendary-quality constant 80 at admission (REQ-008), so the frozen value is guaranteed correct rather than merely unchanged.

prescribed_changes: The exemption is expressed ONCE as a positive category property (exempt_from_quality_bounds, exempt_from_sell_in_decrement) rather than as negated guards restated in front of each of three mutation sites (REQ-004, REQ-005, ANOM-005).

The legacy protection that rested on SEED DATA is replaced by logic. state-machines.json records that Sulfuras 'seeded at SellIn 0 / Quality 80 never even reaches the expiry branch, which means the legendary guard at line 91 is dead code for the seeded data and load-bearing only for a Sulfuras seeded with a negative SellIn' (IL-014, IL-015). REQ-004's second acceptance criterion deliberately exercises that previously unreachable path.
The legendary quality of 80 becomes a validated named constant rather than a value appearing only in seed data (REQ-008, ANOM-006).
state_machines.completeness_check: One state, reachable by definition, intentionally terminal with no exit transitions. This is verified as intentional rather than an oversight: three independent findings (BR-004, BR-005, IL-014) establish that a legendary item is immutable in both dimensions by design, and README.md:24-25 and :44-45 both state it. A machine with no transitions is the correct model.

state_machines.name: RevaluationRunLifecycle
state_machines.description: PRESCRIBED MACHINE WITH NO LEGACY COUNTERPART. The lifecycle of one revaluation cycle bound to one business date. The legacy system has no run concept at all: data-domains.json records the implicit working set as having 'no identity, no run id, no as-of date and no version', and BR-020/IL-017 record no run-date record, no already-processed check and no lock. This machine is what makes REQ-023's idempotence guard enforceable.

states.name: Pending
states.definition: a cycle has been requested for a business date but not yet started
states.description: The authorization check of REQ-026 and the already-completed check of REQ-023 are evaluated here, before any item is read.

states.name: InProgress
states.definition: the cycle is reading and revaluing items
states.description: No other cycle may be InProgress for the same inventory (NFR-010).

states.name: Completed
states.definition: every admitted item has been revalued and the result persisted atomically
states.description: Terminal. Blocks a further non-override cycle for the same business date (REQ-023).

states.name: Failed
states.description: Terminal. The store is left at the full pre-cycle state; no item shows a partially applied cycle (REQ-025). Does NOT block a retry for the same business date.

states.name: Refused
states.definition: the cycle was rejected before any item was modified
states.description: Terminal. Reached on an authorization failure (REQ-026) or an already-completed business date with no override (REQ-023). The refusal is recorded (REQ-027).

transitions.guard: the invoking identity is unauthenticated, or lacks inventory:revalue, or supplied an override without inventory:revalue:override
transitions.action: refuse; modify no item; record the refusal with the identity and reason

traces_to.note: PRESCRIBED — no authorization check of any kind exists in the legacy system.

transitions.trigger: the business date already has a Completed cycle and no override was supplied
transitions.guard: an existing RevaluationRun for this business_date has status Completed
transitions.action: refuse with CYCLE_ALREADY_COMPLETED; modify no item; record the refusal

transitions.trigger: authorization succeeds and the business date is eligible
transitions.guard: identity holds inventory:revalue AND (no Completed cycle exists for this business_date OR a permissioned override with justification was supplied)
transitions.action: record the run with its business date, identity, source reference and override flag; begin reading the inventory source

transitions.trigger: every admitted item has been revalued and the result persisted
transitions.action: record items_read, items_revalued, items_rejected; emit the machine-readable cycle summary; write the audit entries

traces_to.note: PRESCRIBED — the legacy cycle emits and persists nothing.

transitions.trigger: the cycle cannot complete — source unreachable, persistence failure, or concurrent modification detected
transitions.action: roll back to the full pre-cycle state; exit with a non-zero status; record the failure with its error code

traces_to.note: PRESCRIBED. IL-017 records that the legacy system has no failure or retry concept at all, so 'a retry after a partial failure would double-apply a day of depreciation with no way to detect it'.

prescribed_changes: The entire machine is prescribed (REQ-023, ANOM-013). It replaces a legacy temporal model in which, per IL-016, 'a day is defined purely as one call to UpdateQuality' with no clock, no calendar anchor and no record that a day was processed.
state_machines.completeness_check: All five states reachable from Pending. Completed, Failed and Refused are intentionally terminal — a run record is immutable history, and a retry creates a NEW run rather than reopening an old one, which is what makes the uniqueness constraint on (business_date, Completed, override=false) meaningful. Failed deliberately does not block a retry for the same business date; Completed does. That distinction is the substance of REQ-023's idempotence guarantee.

summary.honest_headline: This SRS prescribes 38 requirements over a 172-line application whose entire business logic is 75 lines in one method with zero test coverage. 24 of 28 anomalies are resolved and 4 are deferred with written justification. 15 anomalies require SME confirmation before this document is safe to build from — the largest being whether the application is an FAA system at all (ANOM-028) and whether the missing Conjured rule is a defect or the intended unfinished state of a refactoring kata (ANOM-018). No requirement carries a regulatory obligation, because compliance-citations.json found none applicable.

open_questions: GOVERNING-PROFILE AND APPLICATION-IDENTITY DISCREPANCY (recorded per the binding governing declaration, NOT adopted). This task's governing profile is authoritatively `faa` and this SRS is written under it. But the source tree contains no aviation, NAS, certification or FAA content of any kind — it is the publicly published, MIT-licensed 'Gilded Rose Refactoring Kata' (README.md, attributed to @TerryHughes/@NotMyself at https://github.com/NotMyself/GildedRose) — and src/GildedRose.Console/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:11 and :13 assert AssemblyCompany('DSHS') and Copyright 'DSHS 2015', a third and different agency attribution. Five prior Discovery passes flagged this independently (catalog.json open_questions[0], structural-analysis.json open_questions[0], capability-catalog.json open_questions[0], quality-risk.json top_risk_drivers[5], ux-accessibility.json scope_caveat) and all recommended stakeholder confirmation before downstream use. A stakeholder MUST confirm whether application_id d634afdb-97cc-4589-a080-5766d4f377d5 maps to an FAA-owned production system before Architecture or Modernization consumes this SRS. If it does not, the correct disposition may be retire or replace, in which case this SRS is not the right next artifact. Tracked as ANOM-028.

NO DISCOVERY GATE-APPROVAL STAMP WAS FOUND, SO THE SKILL'S PRECONDITION COULD NOT BE VERIFIED AS STATED. The methodology directs this skill to STOP if any input artifact lacks a gate-approved stamp. No input artifact carries an explicit gate-approval record: the only gate-shaped field in the corpus is ux-accessibility.json's accessibility gate_decision, which reads 'undetermined', and quality-risk.json's escalation-record.json, which records a complexity-escalation disposition rather than a readiness gate. This SRS PROCEEDED on the basis that the orchestrating dispatch staged all eight declared inputs as satisfied prerequisites (per _dispatch-context-discovery-srs-from-discovery.json declared_inputs), which is an inference about the harness, not an observed approval. A reviewer should either supply the gate record or confirm that dispatch staging is the intended gate mechanism. srs.discovery_gate_date is recorded as NOT STAMPED rather than given a fabricated date.

CLIENT PROFILE NOT STAGED — FIVE PRESCRIBED VALUES ARE SUBSTITUTIONS AWAITING RATIFICATION. No profiles/ directory exists in either working directory available to this dispatch, and a search for compliance.yaml returned nothing; capability-catalog.json open_questions[2] independently records the same gap. Consequently: (a) the accessibility standard and conformance level in srs-accessibility-compliance.json are taken second-hand from ux-accessibility.json rather than from profiles/faa/compliance.yaml; (b) NFR-002's target runtime and container substrate prescribe a PROPERTY rather than the profile's named values (prior artifacts cite .NET 8 and Amazon ECS on Fargate in AWS GovCloud); (c) NFR-004's vulnerability action threshold is unstated; (d) NFR-007's complexity limits (cyclomatic 10, nesting depth 3) are conventional static-analysis defaults; (e) NFR-001's 80% coverage baseline is the profile DEFAULT, not a tier-specific target, because no safety tier could be selected. All five must be re-read from the profile and reconciled before Modernization's Extract step.

IS THE MISSING CONJURED RULE A DEFECT OR THE INTENDED UNFINISHED STATE? README.md:34 requires that Conjured items degrade twice as fast, a 'Conjured Mana Cake' sits in live inventory at Program.cs:26, and no implementing branch exists — so the item is mispriced on every run. This SRS prescribes the FIX (REQ-018, plus a whole prescribed state machine and the conversion of the quality floor to a clamp in REQ-003 that it forces). If the business owner rules that this is the kata's intended starting exercise rather than a live defect, REQ-018 is withdrawn, ConjuredGoodsValuationLifecycle is deleted, and ANOM-018 becomes OMIT. This is the single largest conditional in the document. Also unresolved: does the rule match by exact name, by 'Conjured' prefix, or by explicit category attribute as REQ-017 prescribes? BR-MISSING-001 records that the code gives no answer and the codebase has no prefix-matching precedent.

WHO OWNS SIGN-OFF ON THE CHARACTERIZATION TESTS THAT WILL DEFINE CORRECT BEHAVIOUR? structural-analysis.json open_questions[3] asks this directly, naming two specifics: the `Quality = Quality - Quality` branch at Program.cs:99, and whether the 50 quality ceiling is intended to apply to the second and third backstage-pass increments at Program.cs:61-71. Because coverage is 0% and IL-026 records that 'nothing would fail if a re-implementation changed any of them', these tests ARE the specification of legacy behaviour — and NFR-001 requires them to exist and pass before any behaviour-changing requirement is implemented. Without a named owner, the sequencing NFR-001 prescribes has no one to execute it.

DOES A REAL INVENTORY STORE, OR AN UPSTREAM FEED, EXIST OUTSIDE THIS REPOSITORY? structural-analysis.json database-schema-summary asks whether the real production system persists this inventory somewhere owned by another application, warning that 'if it does, that store is invisible to this walk' and that the quality bounds and the legendary 80 invariant 'would need re-checking as data constraints'. structural-analysis.json interface-inventory open_questions[2] separately asks whether an upstream interface feeds the real system. shared-db-analysis.json records the same as RISK-01 at high severity. This bears directly on REQ-022 (where the inventory comes from), REQ-025 (what persistence means) and the whole of srs-data-model.json. Tracked within ANOM-013.

NO DATA OWNER IS DECLARED FOR EITHER DATA DOMAIN. data-domains.json records owner 'UNKNOWN -- not asserted.' for both DD-GRK-001 and DD-GRK-002, and logs it as violation BV-GRK-004 at medium severity. No requirement is generated, because ownership is an organisational fact rather than a code defect — but an unowned data domain has nobody to answer the SME questions in ANOM-002, ANOM-006, ANOM-009, ANOM-011 and ANOM-012, all of which are business-rule rulings. Assigning an owner is a precondition for closing five of the fifteen SME confirmations.

THE REPOSITORY HAS NO USABLE HISTORY, SO NO CHANGE-RATE OR RULE-PROVENANCE EVIDENCE EXISTS. structural-analysis.json open_questions[6] records exactly one git commit ('Update README.md', dated 2017-03-28, no remote configured) and asks whether this is a shallow or re-initialised clone. quality-risk.json consequently EXCLUDED churn_rate from its technical-debt weighting rather than defaulting it to zero. If the real history exists elsewhere it is, as structural-analysis.json puts it, 'the best available source for which rules changed and when' — evidence that would materially improve confidence in the emergent-behaviour rulings (ANOM-006, ANOM-009) by showing whether they were deliberate.

WHO READS THE AUDIT TRAIL, AND WHO ARCHIVES A DEAD ITEM? Two prescribed capabilities have no actor. REQ-027 requires the audit record to be queryable ('a prior valuation is recoverable'), but no auditor or reviewer role could be derived — identity-landscape.json found exactly one actor, 'local-interactive-operator', and no role model of any kind, so naming an auditor would be an invented actor. Likewise REQ-021 prescribes the archival_eligible FLAG but deliberately not the archival ACTION, and ANOM-012 records that the write-off owner is unresolved. Both gaps are stated rather than filled: the actor model in this document has 2 actors because 2 is what the evidence supports, not because 2 is sufficient for the prescribed system. Architecture must commission the missing roles deliberately.

ACCESSIBILITY HAS NO BASELINE AND ITS OBLIGATION IS UNRULED. ux-accessibility.json reports 0 findings and gate_decision 'undetermined' simultaneously: no accessibility checker has ever run (the checker sub-skill's Sub-Skill Output Contract was missing from that agent's dispatch), and whether Section 508 / WCAG 2.1 AA applies to a character-mode non-rendered surface has never been determined. Compounding this, REQ-024 and NFR-002 REMOVE the legacy console surface entirely, so the surface set that must conform is one Architecture has not yet designed — and if it introduces an operator UI for the REQ-023 override or the REQ-021 archival report, that surface has no Discovery baseline whatsoever. Tracked as ANOM-022 and findings A11Y-001/A11Y-002.
